To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the reactivity of spirocyclopentadienones (6-9) is strongly influenced by substituent and con-formational effects, which can be modulated by the presence of a vinylogous acylamide conjugation and the acylation of a nitrogen substituent at C-2, and that the conformational reactivity of the CPI moiety (7) is strongly shape-dependent.

the presence of the vinylogously amide-conjugated 3-amino substituent at C(3) of the cyclohexadienyl ring and the acylation of this amino group with a formyl or an acyl moiety, as well as the ring constraint of this amino group at C(3), are all factors which contribute to the high reactivity of the cyclopropane-containing drugs (1-4).
the reaction of ammonia with the cyclopropenylcyclophane derivative (8) and with the cyclohexadienyl derivative (9) has an activation energy that is about 5 kcal mol(-1), or 2 kcal mol(-1).
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of computational models that allow the rationalization of the experimental observations on the reactivity and selectivity of the duocarmycin and related compounds, and with the prediction of the effect of structural modifications of the CPI moiety on the alkylation reaction.

a detailed theoretical investigation of the uncatalyzed nucleophilic addition reaction of ammonia to a series of spirocyclopentadienone compounds that model the cyclopropenylcyclopropadienone subunits of the antitumor agents CPI (1-3) and duocarmycin SA (4).

the modeling of the substituent and con formational effects on the uncatalyzed reaction of the cyclohexadienones with ammonia, which is the key reaction of the antitumor agents of the duocarmycin family.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reactivity of the cyclohexadienones (6-9) is strongly influenced by both the electronic and steric effects of the substituents and by the conformational flexibility of the molecules.

the cyclopropenylpyrroline (CPI) moiety in duocarmycin is a very reactive species, which is capable of reacting with nucleophiles at a low activation energy, even though it is not the most reactive species among the cyclopropyldienones studied here.
the reactivity of the cyclopropanone subunit in these compounds is strongly influenced by the conformational and substituent effects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the presence of the vinylogously amide-substituted cyclopropyl ring is responsible for the observed reactivity enhancement in the alkylation reactions by ammonia, while the shape-dependent reactivities of the CPI moiety are due to the presence of the 2-acylpyrrolinyl ring.

the reaction mechanism of these compounds is strongly influenced by both the electronic and steric effects of the substituent at the 3-amino group, the ring constraint imposed to the nitrogen atom in 2-position, and by the conformation of the molecule.

the reaction of the parent cyclopropyl cyclohexadienones with amines is an intrinsically slow reaction, which can be accelerated by the presence of an electron-withdrawing substituent at the 2-position of the cyclohexadiene ring, or by a conformational effect, which is operative in the cyclopropyrroloindole derivatives of the CPI family.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the shape dependence of reaction rate in water solution is much more pronounced than in gas phase, and that it is a very important feature in the design of the CPI moiety of antitumor drugs.
conformational control is a key factor in the alkylation reaction of the duocarmycin-type antitumor agents, and it can be used to design new drugs with enhanced reactivity.

the presence of the vinylogously conjugated amide group in cyclopropyl cyclohexadienones (6, 7) is responsible for the high reactivity of these compounds, which is further increased by the presence of a rigid pyrrole ring (10) or by the acylation of a nitrogen substituent (9) at C(2).
